# Cases comparing mkd2xml with kramdown-rfc.
#
# Each case is a small draft, followed by what mkd2xml must make of it:
# either parts of the XML, or an error.
#
# The XML here was not written by hand. For every case that expects XML,
# mkd2xml's output and that of kramdown-rfc 1.7.43 were both prepared with
# "xml2rfc --prep" (3.34.1) and compared element by element, and they were
# the same. So these cases record where the two tools are known to agree,
# and a change to one of them means that agreement has to be checked again.
#
# Two cases are exceptions, "angle_text" and "code_special": kramdown-rfc's
# own output for them is not valid XML. There the expected XML is what
# mkd2xml produces, checked only to be accepted by xml2rfc.
#
# The cases that expect an error are constructs that kramdown-rfc and a
# CommonMark parser read differently, or that mkd2xml does not support.
# Refusing them is what keeps mkd2xml from producing XML that is quietly
# different from kramdown-rfc's.
#
# Format: "%% case NAME KIND" starts a case. KIND is "body" when the text is
# appended to the standard front matter in the test, "full" when it is the
# whole file, and "quoted" when the whole file is given as one JSON string
# because its exact bytes matter. "%% want PART" starts an expectation,
# where PART is "error" or the XML element to compare.

%% case adj_fence_fence body
Intro:

~~~
a
~~~
~~~
b
~~~
%% want middle
  <middle>
    <section anchor="introduction">
      <name>Introduction</name>
      <t>Intro:</t>
      <artwork><![CDATA[
a
]]></artwork>
      <artwork><![CDATA[
b
]]></artwork>
    </section>
  </middle>
%% want back
  <back>
  </back>
%% case adj_fence_para body
Intro:

~~~
code
~~~
After.
%% want middle
  <middle>
    <section anchor="introduction">
      <name>Introduction</name>
      <t>Intro:</t>
      <artwork><![CDATA[
code
]]></artwork>
      <t>After.</t>
    </section>
  </middle>
%% want back
  <back>
  </back>
%% case adj_heading_fence body

~~~

  <back>
  </back>

        </li>
        <li>
          <t>b</t>
        </li>
      </ul>
    </section>
  </middle>

  <back>
  </back>

%% case back_appendix body
Text.

--- back

# An Appendix

A.

## Sub Appendix

B.

# Acknowledgments
{:numbered="false"}

Thanks.
%% want middle
  <middle>
    <section anchor="introduction">
      <name>Introduction</name>
      <t>Text.</t>
    </section>
  </middle>
%% want back
  <back>
    <section anchor="an-appendix">
      <name>An Appendix</name>
      <t>A.</t>
      <section anchor="sub-appendix">
        <name>Sub Appendix</name>
        <t>B.</t>
      </section>
    </section>
    <section numbered="false" anchor="acknowledgments">
      <name>Acknowledgments</name>
      <t>Thanks.</t>
    </section>
  </back>
%% case back_empty body
Text.

--- back
%% want middle
  <middle>
    <section anchor="introduction">
      <name>Introduction</name>
      <t>Text.</t>
    </section>
  </middle>
%% want back
  <back>
  </back>
%% case bcp14 body
{::boilerplate bcp14-tagged}

You MUST, MUST NOT, (SHOULD), MAY. MUSTARD is not; must is not. **MUST** and *SHOULD*. In `MUST` code. NOT RECOMMENDED and RECOMMENDED, SHALL NOT, REQUIRED, OPTIONAL.
It SHOULD
NOT break.
%% want middle
  <middle>
    <section anchor="introduction">
      <name>Introduction</name>
      <t>The key words "<bcp14>MUST</bcp14>", "<bcp14>MUST NOT</bcp14>", "<bcp14>REQUIRED</bcp14>", "<bcp14>SHALL</bcp14>", "<bcp14>SHALL NOT</bcp14>", "<bcp14>SHOULD</bcp14>", "<bcp14>SHOULD NOT</bcp14>", "<bcp14>RECOMMENDED</bcp14>", "<bcp14>NOT RECOMMENDED</bcp14>", "<bcp14>MAY</bcp14>", and "<bcp14>OPTIONAL</bcp14>" in this document are to be interpreted as described in BCP&#xA0;14 <xref target="RFC2119"/> <xref target="RFC8174"/> when, and only when, they appear in all capitals, as shown here.</t>
      <t>You <bcp14>MUST</bcp14>, <bcp14>MUST NOT</bcp14>, (<bcp14>SHOULD</bcp14>), <bcp14>MAY</bcp14>. MUSTARD is not; must is not. <strong><bcp14>MUST</bcp14></strong> and <em><bcp14>SHOULD</bcp14></em>. In <tt>MUST</tt> code. <bcp14>NOT RECOMMENDED</bcp14> and <bcp14>RECOMMENDED</bcp14>, <bcp14>SHALL NOT</bcp14>, <bcp14>REQUIRED</bcp14>, <bcp14>OPTIONAL</bcp14>.
It <bcp14>SHOULD
NOT</bcp14> break.</t>
    </section>
  </middle>
%% want back
  <back>
    <references anchor="sec-normative-references">
      <name>Normative References</name>
      <reference anchor="RFC2119"/>
      <reference anchor="RFC8174"/>
    </references>
  </back>
%% case bcp14_heading body
{::boilerplate bcp14-tagged}

# What You MUST Do

You MUST.

* item MUST
%% want middle
  <middle>
    <section anchor="introduction">
      <name>Introduction</name>
      <t>The key words "<bcp14>MUST</bcp14>", "<bcp14>MUST NOT</bcp14>", "<bcp14>REQUIRED</bcp14>", "<bcp14>SHALL</bcp14>", "<bcp14>SHALL NOT</bcp14>", "<bcp14>SHOULD</bcp14>", "<bcp14>SHOULD NOT</bcp14>", "<bcp14>RECOMMENDED</bcp14>", "<bcp14>NOT RECOMMENDED</bcp14>", "<bcp14>MAY</bcp14>", and "<bcp14>OPTIONAL</bcp14>" in this document are to be interpreted as described in BCP&#xA0;14 <xref target="RFC2119"/> <xref target="RFC8174"/> when, and only when, they appear in all capitals, as shown here.</t>
    </section>
    <section anchor="what-you-must-do">
      <name>What You MUST Do</name>
      <t>You <bcp14>MUST</bcp14>.</t>
      <ul spacing="normal">
        <li>
          <t>item <bcp14>MUST</bcp14></t>
        </li>
      </ul>
    </section>
  </middle>
%% want back
  <back>
    <references anchor="sec-normative-references">
      <name>Normative References</name>
      <reference anchor="RFC2119"/>
      <reference anchor="RFC8174"/>
    </references>
  </back>
%% case bcp14_lists body
{::boilerplate bcp14-tagged}

1. Clients MUST do it.

   * Servers SHOULD NOT.

2. It MAY.
%% want middle
  <middle>
    <section anchor="introduction">
      <name>Introduction</name>
      <t>The key words "<bcp14>MUST</bcp14>", "<bcp14>MUST NOT</bcp14>", "<bcp14>REQUIRED</bcp14>", "<bcp14>SHALL</bcp14>", "<bcp14>SHALL NOT</bcp14>", "<bcp14>SHOULD</bcp14>", "<bcp14>SHOULD NOT</bcp14>", "<bcp14>RECOMMENDED</bcp14>", "<bcp14>NOT RECOMMENDED</bcp14>", "<bcp14>MAY</bcp14>", and "<bcp14>OPTIONAL</bcp14>" in this document are to be interpreted as described in BCP&#xA0;14 <xref target="RFC2119"/> <xref target="RFC8174"/> when, and only when, they appear in all capitals, as shown here.</t>
      <ol spacing="normal" type="1">
        <li>
          <t>Clients <bcp14>MUST</bcp14> do it.</t>
          <ul spacing="normal">
            <li>
              <t>Servers <bcp14>SHOULD NOT</bcp14>.</t>
            </li>
          </ul>
        </li>
        <li>
          <t>It <bcp14>MAY</bcp14>.</t>
        </li>
      </ol>
    </section>
  </middle>
%% want back
  <back>
    <references anchor="sec-normative-references">
      <name>Normative References</name>
      <reference anchor="RFC2119"/>
      <reference anchor="RFC8174"/>
    </references>
  </back>

      <t>You MUST and SHOULD NOT.</t>

%% case bracket_ref_like body
See [RFC8555] for details {{!RFC8555}}.

%% case file_bom quoted

Intro:

1) one
2) two
%% want error
a numbered list must be written "1." and not "1)"
%% case list_ordered_same body
Intro:

1. one
1. two
1. three
%% want middle
  <middle>
    <section anchor="introduction">
      <name>Introduction</name>
      <t>Intro:</t>
      <ol spacing="normal" type="1">
        <li>
          <t>one</t>
        </li>
        <li>
          <t>two</t>
        </li>
        <li>
          <t>three</t>
        </li>
      </ol>
    </section>
  </middle>
%% want back
  <back>
  </back>
%% case list_ordered_start body
Intro:

3. three
4. four
%% want error
a numbered list must start at 1; kramdown-rfc would renumber this one from 1
%% case list_then_para body
Intro:

* a
* b

After the list.
%% want middle
  <middle>
    <section anchor="introduction">
      <name>Introduction</name>
      <t>Intro:</t>
      <ul spacing="normal">
        <li>
          <t>a</t>
        </li>
        <li>
          <t>b</t>
        </li>
      </ul>
      <t>After the list.</t>
    </section>
  </middle>
%% want back
  <back>
  </back>
%% case list_tight body
Intro:

* a
* b
* c
%% want middle
  <middle>
    <section anchor="introduction">
      <name>Introduction</name>
      <t>Intro:</t>
      <ul spacing="normal">
        <li>
          <t>a</t>
        </li>
        <li>
          <t>b</t>
        </li>
        <li>
          <t>c</t>
        </li>
      </ul>
    </section>
  </middle>
%% want back
  <back>
  </back>
%% case math body
Inline $$a^2$$ math.
%% want error
"$$" would be read by kramdown-rfc as math, which is not supported
%% case multi_blank body
Para one.



Para two.
%% want middle
  <middle>
    <section anchor="introduction">
      <name>Introduction</name>
      <t>Para one.</t>
      <t>Para two.</t>
    </section>
  </middle>
%% want back
  <back>
  </back>
%% case not_a_list body
1986\. A great year.

2 * 3 is six.
%% want middle

    <section anchor="introduction">
      <name>Introduction</name>
      <t>1986. A great year.</t>
      <t>2 * 3 is six.</t>
    </section>
  </middle>
%% want back
  <back>
  </back>
%% case num_dot_text body
In 2019. Something. 3.14 is pi. v1.2.3 ok.
%% want middle

    <section anchor="introduction">
      <name>Introduction</name>
      <t>In 2019. Something. 3.14 is pi. v1.2.3 ok.</t>
    </section>
  </middle>
%% want back
  <back>
  </back>
%% case para_starts_special body
\# not a heading

+1 for this.

- - -

-5 degrees.
%% want error
unsupported Markdown construct (ThematicBreak)
%% case pipe_text body
a | b | c in text.
%% want error
"|" in text would be read by kramdown-rfc as a table; write "\|", or put the text in backticks
%% case plus_minus_text body
A + B - C = D, +1, -1, a - b.
%% want middle
  <middle>
    <section anchor="introduction">
      <name>Introduction</name>
      <t>A + B - C = D, +1, -1, a - b.</t>
    </section>
  </middle>
%% want back
  <back>
  </back>
%% case quote_chars body
He said "hi" -- and 'bye' ... `code "q" -- x` done.
%% want middle
  <middle>
    <section anchor="introduction">
      <name>Introduction</name>
      <t>He said "hi" -- and 'bye' ... <tt>code "q" -- x</tt> done.</t>
    </section>
  </middle>
%% want back
  <back>
  </back>
%% case refs_both body
First {{!RFC8555}} then {{?RFC8555}} and {{?RFC2119}} then {{!RFC2119}}.
%% want middle
  <middle>
    <section anchor="introduction">
      <name>Introduction</name>
      <t>First <xref target="RFC8555"/> then <xref target="RFC8555"/> and <xref target="RFC2119"/> then <xref target="RFC2119"/>.</t>
    </section>
  </middle>
%% want back
  <back>
    <references anchor="sec-normative-references">
      <name>Normative References</name>
      <reference anchor="RFC8555"/>
      <reference anchor="RFC2119"/>
    </references>
  </back>
%% case section_empty body
Text.

# Empty One

# After Empty

x
%% want middle

      <name>Introduction</name>
      <t>Text.</t>
    </section>

      <name>After Empty</name>
      <t>x</t>
    </section>

%% want back

  </back>
%% case section_only_list body
Text.

# Codey

~~~
x

    <section anchor="introduction">

      <t>Text.</t>
    </section>

        <li>
          <t>a</t>
        </li>
        <li>
          <t>b</t>
        </li>
      </ul>
    </section>
    <section anchor="codey">
      <name>Codey</name>
      <artwork><![CDATA[
x
]]></artwork>
    </section>
  </middle>
%% want back
  <back>
  </back>

A *.example.org wildcard and a**b and f(*args).
%% want error

%% want error

  </back>
%% case xml_passthrough body
Text.

<aside><t>An aside.</t></aside>
%% want error
unsupported Markdown construct (HTMLBlock)
%% case xref_format body
See {{<<introduction}} and {{<introduction}}.
%% want error
unsupported cross-reference {{<<introduction}}
%% case xref_forms body
See {{!RFC8555}}, {{?RFC2119}}, {{RFC8555, Section 7.3}}, {{Section 8.1 of RFC8555}}, {{RFC8555 (Appendix A.1)}} and {{introduction}}.
%% want middle
  <middle>
    <section anchor="introduction">
      <name>Introduction</name>
      <t>See <xref target="RFC8555"/>, <xref target="RFC2119"/>, <xref section="7.3" sectionFormat="comma" target="RFC8555"/>, <xref section="8.1" sectionFormat="of" target="RFC8555"/>, <xref section="A.1" sectionFormat="parens" target="RFC8555"/> and <xref target="introduction"/>.</t>
    </section>
  </middle>
%% want back
  <back>
    <references anchor="sec-combined-references">
      <name>References</name>
      <references anchor="sec-normative-references">
        <name>Normative References</name>
        <reference anchor="RFC8555"/>
      </references>
      <references anchor="sec-informative-references">
        <name>Informative References</name>
        <reference anchor="RFC2119"/>
      </references>
    </references>
  </back>
%% case xref_in_emph body
This is *really in {{!RFC8555}}* and `{{RFC8555}}` in code.
%% want middle
  <middle>
    <section anchor="introduction">
      <name>Introduction</name>
      <t>This is <em>really in <xref target="RFC8555"/></em> and <tt>{{RFC8555}}</tt> in code.</t>
    </section>
  </middle>
%% want back
  <back>
    <references anchor="sec-normative-references">
      <name>Normative References</name>
      <reference anchor="RFC8555"/>
    </references>
  </back>
%% case xref_sections_multi body
See {{Sections 7.3 and 8.1 of RFC8555}}. Also {{!RFC8555}}.
%% want error
unsupported cross-reference {{Sections 7.3 and 8.1 of RFC8555}}
%% case xref_text body

%% want error
unsupported cross-reference {{RFC8555 (the ACME spec)}}
